newsitem.title: CHINA: China M2 up 26.8 percent at end-Sept-central bank.
newsitem.headline: China M2 up 26.8 percent at end-Sept-central bank.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply rose by a year-on-year 26.8 percent at the end of the third quarter to 7.2042 trillion yuan, the central bank said in a report published in the Financial News on Thursday.
China has set a goal of 25 percent growth for M2 for this year, down from 29.5 percent in 1995.

China's M1, or cash in circulation plus current deposits, rose by a year-on-year 17.1 percent at the end of September to 2.6336 trillion yuan, the bank said. It has set a goal of no more than 18 percent for this year.

The month-on-month September increase in M1 growth from 15.1 percent at the end of of August reflected the growing payment ability of enterprises, Governor of the People's Bank of China Dai Xianglong told Reuters in an interview this week.
M0, or cash in circulation, grew by a year-on-year 14.1 percent at the end of September to 840.9 billion yuan.

Sales of consumer goods increased by 2.0 percentage points in September compared with August and this indicated that the bank's two cuts in interest rates this year had helped to promote sales of goods and reduced stockpiles, Dai said.
